title: The Cube Researchers
subtitle: Only by opening it can we know what's inside—but should we really?

trails.title: Quantifying Pain
trails.description: Can the sum of the mind and the spirit be reduced to scientific data?

content.text:
Classification: High
Patient Codename: Moth
Medical Record:
Examination reveals that the patient, having returned from the Antarctic Operation, performed repeated identity overwrites throughout their long-term undercover assignment, exceeding the safe iteration threshold. The patient's Phototaxis now shows multiple unstable segments, which may affect overwrite efficacy and increase the risk of personality collapse.
Brainwave activity shows an increase in fast waves, indicating compensatory neuronal overload. Neurotransmitter concentrations are imbalanced: dopamine levels have dropped to 60% of the normal range, and serotonin synthesis efficiency has decreased by 28%. Physical damage is present in the medial prefrontal cortex, with mild edema in the limbic system ...
...
The patient also overextended her use of arcane skills during the Antarctic Operation, resulting in prolonged pneuma depletion. Recovery prospects are not encouraging. Strict limits must be placed on her arcane skill usage in the near term to prevent irreversible damage.
During psychological evaluation, the patient exhibited mild self-perception disorder ...
...
Diagnosis:
The patient's brain damage is largely within controllable limits. Although a deep personality overwrite should be performed upon completion of the undercover assignment, given the critical enemy intelligence and knowledge obtained during this infiltration of Manus Vindictae, an unconventional approach has been approved: the Phototaxis overwrite will be suspended for the time being. The patient will instead receive regular injections of neural repair peptides to maintain brain function. During this period, the patient's psychological state must be closely monitored to confirm the results of cognitive anchoring.

items.text: The Cube Researchers
Countdown to the "Storm"

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You still look pale, Ms. Stranger.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Well enough to get back to work. Thank you for your concern.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Though, before we exchange any more pleasantries, shall we allow this researcher to finish her job first?
She glances over to the other woman standing in the corner.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: Hello, Timekeeper. You're as punctual as ever, right down to the tick.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: In fact, you're early, miss. But I must confess, I was never all that timely before becoming the Timekeeper.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: Oh, wow, and a sense of humor too! You've really got it all, Ms. Vertin.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: I'll be the one conducting research into your Suitcase's technology this time. Well, it's not just me, of course; it'll go to the team. One researcher alone couldn't possibly understand a device of the Suitcase's magnitude, could they?

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: So, has everyone moved out already?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. They're all in the Foundation's guest rooms. I've checked every nook and cranny to ensure no one was left behind.
This year's Suitcase inspection just so happens to fall during the "Storm." Perhaps Team Timekeeper will be able to take a vacation.
Following protocol, the technician takes the emptied Suitcase.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: Thank you for your cooperation. I'm sure this will help us learn more about that mysterious Spinning Wheel.
She holds the Suitcase delicately, almost reverently. She stares down at it and then glances up again, as if weighing unspoken words on her tongue.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hm? Anything else I can help you with?

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: Um, Timekeeper, there's something I'd like to ask you about, kind of a private matter.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: About the Amber Room. I heard you went through some kind of time distortion in there. Is that true?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. It was exactly as I wrote in my report.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: Time distortion ... If only I were assigned to research that! What could be more fun than studying time itself!
Her visible excitement is contained—if just barely—by concern for the marvelous device she is holding.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: Not to knock working on the Suitcase, which I suppose involves the study of space ... Space or time, ah, I wonder which is deeper.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: You know, you're a real gatherer of mysteries, Timekeeper. Actually, you're kind of a mystery yourself. *sigh* I don't know what I'm saying.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: Sorry for the blabbering. I should really go.

items.speaker: Technician
items.text: We'll get the Suitcase back to you in a few days. A week at most. Please plan your schedule accordingly. Goodbye, Timekeeper.
She nods, causing the light to reflect off her sleek mask, then makes her exit.
Ms. Stranger approaches gently.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I wonder if she even saw me or Ms. Sonetto. Laplace really does excel in finding "unique" talents.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm used to it.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Has the Foundation assigned you a new job already? I thought you'd want to rest for a while longer.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I wish I could, but it's not my decision to make.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The Foundation received your report on the Don Operation while I was still stuck in bed. It mentioned that Igor gave you a "boon."

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Part of my work involves studying the Manus's arcane skills, so I was sent to Laplace to help.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The project leader said they've made some progress already, but they'll need your help to continue.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Which is why I invited you here.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Is the research team here at the Foundation?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Yes. The project leader and her assistant were notified in advance and brought their equipment here.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Follow me. They asked for an open space, so we agreed to meet in the garden.
Southern Garden, St. Pavlov Foundation
Cold white auxiliary buildings form an uneven enclosure around the pleasant green commons of the Foundation's southern annex.
The patterns of shrubbery and lace-like walkways resemble, in a deliberate way, the intricate gardens that surround the Palace of Versailles—albeit tightly compacted.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: I don't understand how one can relax while walking through a maze like this.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The view was much more enjoyable before the hedges grew into walls like this.
At the center of the commons stands a peculiar instrument.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: That should be them over there. Is that Eagle?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Hi, Ms. Timekeeper, Ms. Sonetto, Ms. Stranger.
The girl nods dutifully, but bounds back with a bright smile.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: It's great to see you again.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's been a while, Eagle. I understand you've joined Laplace.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Will you be working on this project too?

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Not exactly. The project leader is my tutor. I'm just here to help with a few things. She is ...
Hello, Timekeeper. It's truly an honor.
A woman steps out from behind the device. At a glance, she could be mistaken for any other Laplace researcher, save for the sharp and cunning look in her eyes.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: I hope you've found the time to read Ms. Recoleta's novel.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Oh, you can call me Marguerite.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's a pleasure, Marguerite.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Your timing's perfect. Eagle and I have just finished setting up the Omni-Vector Virtual Monitoring Device. We're ready to start the experiment at any time.
She presents the device to them with a look that reveals both anticipation and calculation in a single dangerous smile.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Please, take a seat, Timekeeper. You're about to experience quite the adventure.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Wait, Ms. Marguerite. Would you mind explaining what this "Omni-Vector Virtual Monitoring Device" is before you start?

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It's a "Chaos-System Omni-Vector Quantitative Analysis and Spatial-Metric Virtual Sensory Monitoring Device," to be precise.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Based on what we know about this cube, it'll go through unpredictable changes in the near future. So, to keep it under control, we must—

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Ah. Judging by your faces, I think I haven't been clear enough.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Allow me to make things easier for everyone.

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Using the data I provided, the research team has decoded the arcane skill Manus Vindictae used to stabilize the shell of the "boon," allowing us to access what was held inside.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It was trivial, really. All we needed to do was listen.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: So you're saying I can use this device to "hear" what's inside the cube.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Exactly. I know it isn't quite correct to call it a "monitoring device," but language itself is an exercise in uncertainty, wouldn't you say?

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: Given that the cube was created by Arcana, a less direct but safer method of exploration is probably for the best.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: As it happens, I already attempted to listen to the device while setting up the system. As soon as the first blast of sound reached my ears, I was hit with a wave of dizziness and briefly fell unconscious.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Symptoms that closely resemble what I experienced when you secretly "invited" me to the lake in your Suitcase.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It's likely, Vertin, that you are the only one able to remain conscious while listening to the device. And don't worry. Eagle has already booked a VIP room for you at the rehab center, just in case.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I see. Well, I suppose there's only one way to find out.
The hat is removed, allowing the head to fit more easily inside the dome.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Virtual environmental model constructed. You may begin at any time.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Ms. Stranger, place the Pandora's box on the tray, if you would.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Just as I predicted, the cube appears to be a superposition of ever-changing matter.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It seems feasible to quantify the system using chaos theory. The continuity observed in the data aligns well with our simulated outcomes. Wait—

items.speaker: Ms. Stranger
items.text: The Timekeeper seems unwell.
The ringing in the ears fades, only to be replaced by the wailing of the device's alarm.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The machine is smoking. Did something go wrong?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Timekeeper! Are you alright?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm fine. My ears are ringing, but that's all.
The hat is put back on, concealing still-spinning eyes beneath its brim.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: So you were able to withstand whatever's inside the cube, as expected, but it looks like our monitoring device wasn't.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: The overload of chaos data caused it to break down, though it should've been fine under the protection of the Apeiron scroll.
Eagle diligently jots down notes as she provides a full assessment of the damage.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Did you hear anything during the experiment?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I did. But I don't quite know how to describe it. It was almost like the sound of sinking quicksand?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I think I've made contact with similar powers before. I'm not sure what it is, but I know it could be very dangerous.

items.speaker: Eagle
items.text: Then Ms. Stranger was right. It could be risky to break the shell before we find out what's inside.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It's still an option worth considering, since we've gotten nothing from the monitoring device.
She lets the undertone of excitement bleed into her voice intentionally as she focuses her attention on the artifact.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Well, Timekeeper? Shall we open it?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No. The risk is too high.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Shame. Anyway, if you change your mind ...
She produces a capsule-shaped item.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: Use this. Our virtual neighbor came up with this capsule while we were working on the monitoring device.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: It activates with a simple incantation. It'll take about seven seconds to dissolve the shell. After that, who knows what might happen.

items.speaker: Marguerite
items.text: I'll teach you the incantation later. It's easy, as long as you passed the SPDM's ninth-grade arcane skills class.
Accept

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: Thank you. I'll treat it with the utmost care.

branch.speaker: Marguerite
branch.text: Good. I look forward to hearing its secrets. If you decide to open it, that is.

items.text: Talk about ninth grade

branch.speaker: Vertin
branch.text: As it happens, I wasn't in class for most of ninth grade.

branch.speaker: Marguerite
branch.text: Really? Either way, I'm sure being the Timekeeper has given you more than enough experience to handle it.

items.text: Marguerite hands over the capsule with a practiced smile.
